x: KodaCode runs AI coding agents on your code, on your machine, with the models you choose. It isn't a chat window attached to an editor. It gives the agent a map of your code, a memory of what it learned, and rules about what it may touch. Then it shows every step that the agent takes.

Ask for the work in Plan mode . The agent proposes a plan: each step, the files it will touch, and how it will check the result. Ask for a revision as often as you like. An automation reads part of a project and asks a decision model typed questions about it. Then it acts on the answers: it records a note or starts an agent session. It can run manually or on a schedule. Open Automations with /automations or ⇧⌘R.

Automation What it does risky-change-review Reviews the latest commit when it is risky or touches sensitive code secret-leak-check Catches a key, token or password added in the latest commit untested-change Notices changed functions that no test reaches dependency-change-watch Examines a dependency that the latest commit adds, and any known vulnerability it brings docs-drift Flags a change the REA

An automation has five parts: Read : what it reads. Inputs are the git diff, untested changes, schema changes, a file, a read-only command, a dependency scan or a secret scan. State : a template that puts the inputs together for the decision model. Ask : typed questions, answered yes/no or on a scale, each with a confidence. Decide : rules, checked in order. Memory is on by default ( Preferences → Memory → Use memory ). Before each turn, KodaCode recalls the memories that match your message and gives them to the agent. The first message of a session also gets a briefing of the project's recent activity, open problems and patterns. The agent sees the recalled memories and the briefing. The transcript does not show them. The agent decides what to store.

A memory has a type, a title, content, tags and an importance from 0 to 1. Its type is one of task, code pattern, problem, solution, project, technology, error, fix, command, file context, workflow, general, conversation or preference. A memory counts as read when the agent gets it or lists its related memories. A recall or a search does not count. Recent in project lists the memories that changed last. Manage opens the Memory screen. Click a memory to open it there.

Each project keeps its memories in .koda/memory/ , which git ignores. If you choose it in project setup, the project keeps them in .koda/memory.json instead. That file is committed with the repository, so your team shares it.
The agent's memory tool stores, gets, updates and deletes memories. It also searches and recalls memories, lists related memories, links memories and shows recent activity.

A turn retries rate limits, overloads, server errors and dropped connections by itself. It makes 3 attempts. Then, when the provider is down, it makes up to 5 recovery waits of 15 to 60 seconds. Raise or lower both in General settings . Test Connection on the provider checks the key or sign-in. /logs shows what failed.
Model calls per turn (100 by default) caps how often one turn may call the model. Disable the limit so that a turn runs until the model is done.

The status in the top bar says why: Needs approval (an approval card is at the bottom of the transcript), a question, or a plan. The sessions dock lists the sessions that wait for you under Attention .
Commands yield after 10 seconds and keep running. The prompt box's dock lists them. Use Stop for one command, or Stop all . Esc stops the turn but leaves its commands running.

Choose the models in Crew Workflow first. /crew-supervised needs a Leader model and a Worker model . /crew-self-managed needs a Worker model . The project must be a git repository with at least one commit. No merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert can be in progress, and the working tree cannot have unresolved conflicts.
You can't merge or discard a goal while a command that it polls is running. If your project changed under it, merging leaves the project as it was, and the goal says what blocked the merge.
Code graph can't watch this path in the status bar means that the code graph doesn't see file changes there as they happen.
Settings, sessions and logs live in ~/.config/kc . Keys and sign-ins are in the system keychain. See Files & folders .
